Body: Changing the positional arg type from `number` to `string` can affect CLI behavior/documentation and shell completion (users may now pass non-numeric values that previously failed at parsing time). If yargs supports it in this project setup, consider adding `coerce`/`transform`/`check` (or equivalent) to validate at argument-parsing time while still allowing `#123`, so invalid values fail before running the command handler.

The tests cover many invalid strings, but they don’t cover a few important boundary cases implied by `parsePrNumber`’s implementation: values with a plus sign (`+3`), internal whitespace (`# 992`), and very large numbers beyond `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (which `/^\\d+$/` accepts but can round). Adding explicit expectations for those cases would lock in intended behavior and prevent silent precision bugs.

`expandHome()` can be bypassed into an unintended absolute path when the remainder begins with a path separator, because `path.join(homedir(), "/etc")` (or `"\\Windows"`) discards the home prefix. For example, `"~//etc/passwd"` becomes `"/etc/passwd"` on POSIX. To keep the “escape-safe” guarantee stated in the docstring, strip any leading separators from the sliced remainder before joining (and add a regression test for `"~//..."` and Windows variants like `"~\\\\..."`).

The comment says “escape checks below run against the expanded path”, but the actual escape check still only runs for non-absolute paths. After this change, `~/...` becomes absolute and bypasses the `FSUtil.contains(location.directory, ...)` gate entirely, which can materially change the sandboxing behavior for reads. If reads are intended to remain confined to `location.directory`, add an equivalent confinement check for (tilde-expanded) absolute paths; if reading outside is intended, consider updating the comment and/or error semantics so it’s clear the guard is only for relative-path escapes.

Tilde-expansion behavior is now part of `grep`’s input-path handling, but the added tests only cover `FSUtil.expandHome`, `LocationMutation.resolve`, and `ReadTool`. Add a focused test for `grep` (and similarly for `glob` / ripgrep-backed search) that asserts `~`/`~/...` is expanded and that any existing path-boundary/escape behavior remains unchanged.

The table column alignment spacing for this row is inconsistent with the other rows (extra padding in the model name and ID columns). This can reduce readability in Markdown tables. Consider normalizing spacing to match the surrounding entries (typically single spaces around column separators) so the table renders consistently.

The markdown table uses a double leading pipe (`||`), which typically renders as an extra empty column (or can render incorrectly depending on the MDX/markdown renderer). Use a single leading pipe per row (e.g., `| Flag | Description |`) to ensure the table renders consistently.

`parseFloat` will mis-order versions like `gpt-5.10` (parsed as `5.1`), incorrectly treating it as older than `5.4`. Prefer comparing major/minor numerically (e.g., parse major/minor as integers and compare tuples) rather than using floating-point parsing for dotted versions.

Parameter name `apiID` is inconsistent with the more common `...Id` casing used elsewhere (e.g., `accountId`, `providerID` in this codebase). Consider renaming to `apiId` for consistency and readability.

Changing this default will affect any user/environment where the `showCustomAgents` key is absent (e.g., existing installs prior to the setting being introduced, cleared storage, first-run). If the intent is to enable broadly, consider adding a settings migration/versioning step to explicitly set the value for existing users (so behavior is controlled and auditable), or gate the default behind a feature flag/remote config if rollout needs to be managed.

`coerce` conditionally returns either a `number` or the original (typically `string`) value, and then the handler parses again anyway. This makes the effective type of `args.number` harder to reason about and duplicates logic. Consider removing the `coerce` and parsing once in the handler, or alternatively make `coerce` the single source of truth (e.g., throw/return a consistently typed value) and avoid re-parsing downstream.

`parsePrNumber` explicitly accepts `string | number`, but the added tests only cover string inputs. Add at least one test case that passes a numeric input (e.g., `992`, `0`, `-3`, `12.5`) to ensure numeric callers behave as intended and to prevent regressions if yargs (or other callers) provide a number.

The table rows start with `||`, which typically renders as an empty first column (or can break table rendering depending on the markdown pipeline). Use a single leading `|` for standard markdown tables so the table renders consistently.

The test name says “keeps duplicate separators”, but the expectation uses `path.join(...)`, which normalizes separators (i.e., it does **not** keep duplicates). Please rename the test to reflect the actual behavior (e.g., “normalizes duplicate separators after `~/`”) or adjust the assertion/implementation if preserving duplicates is truly intended.

`readCalls` is shared mutable state across tests. If Bun/effect tests run concurrently (now or in the future), this can cause cross-test interference. Consider making `readCalls` per-test (e.g., `let readCalls: AbsolutePath[]` reset by reassignment in `beforeEach`, or constructing the `reader` layer inside each test / a helper that closes over a fresh array) so parallelism can’t corrupt assertions.

The doc comment claims “escape-safe”, but `join(homedir(), ...)` normalizes `..` segments (e.g., `~/../x` can expand outside the home directory). If that behavior is acceptable (likely), please clarify the comment to avoid implying this prevents traversal; it only rewrites the `~` prefix and does not enforce containment within the home directory.

`homedir()` is called up to 3 times per invocation. Consider caching it in a local `const home = homedir()` to avoid repeated syscalls/IO (minor, but easy to improve) and to keep the function simpler to read.

`onAfterLoad` is invoked before checking whether the session ID changed while `loadMore` was in-flight. If the user navigates to a different session during the await, `restoreHistoryAnchor()` can run against the new session's scroller with a stale captured anchor, causing an incorrect scroll adjustment.

Markdown copy buttons are preserved by returning `false` in `morphdom`'s `onBeforeElUpdated`, but their `aria-label`/`data-tooltip` never get refreshed when the i18n labels change (or when copied state needs to be reflected on the preserved node). This can leave stale accessibility text/tooltips.

For streaming code blocks, the existing DOM is updated in-place, but the associated copy button's `aria-label`/tooltip are not updated when labels change (e.g. language switch). Since the copy button is intentionally kept mounted, update its attributes/state alongside token updates.

For empty bracketed-paste content, the handler now always returns without initiating any fallback paste behavior unless an image is detected. Previously this path dispatched `prompt.paste`; with the current code, a Windows Terminal empty paste that is not an image (or if clipboard read fails/returns text) becomes a no-op. Consider restoring a fallback (e.g., dispatching `keymap.dispatchCommand(\"prompt.paste\")`) when no image attachment is produced.

This introduces an `await` (async boundary) before calling `event.preventDefault()` in the empty-paste path. If the terminal performs its default paste behavior while awaiting `clipboard.read`, the app may end up with duplicated/undesired insertion. To keep behavior consistent with the non-empty path, call `event.preventDefault()` before any `await` in the paste handler path where you intend to fully own paste insertion (including the image-clipboard detection flow).

Using `execSync` with a single interpolated command string runs through a shell and embeds `file` directly into the command text. This is brittle (quoting/escaping issues) and increases command-injection risk compared to invoking the executable with an args array. Prefer `execFileSync`/`spawn`/the existing `command(...)` helper with explicit arguments (e.g., `osascript` with multiple `-e` args) so paths are not shell-interpreted.

Switching to `execSync` here blocks the Node event loop while PowerShell runs (up to the 10s timeout). In a TUI, this can freeze rendering/input handling during clipboard reads. Consider using the existing async `command(...)` helper (spawn-based) to keep the UI responsive, while still applying a timeout/kill strategy if needed.

When `bundle-artifact` is provided, the subsequent `git fetch "${BRANCH}.bundle" ...` requires that the prerequisite commits (excluded via `^origin/dev` when creating the bundle) exist locally. With `actions/checkout`'s default shallow clone, the base commit may be missing, causing `git fetch <bundle>` to fail with missing prerequisites if `dev` advances between bundling and this job. Use a full fetch for the compute job to make bundle checkouts reliable.

Valid, thanks. The explicit base fetch does not unshallow an actions/checkout clone, so an advanced dev tip can leave the bundle prerequisite missing. Updated the compute checkout to use fetch-depth: 0.

`expectedBunVersionRange` is now only a lower bound (`>=1.3.0`), which also allows bun 1.4.x/2.x. That contradicts the comment/PR intent (“only major.minor bound”) and could permit incompatible future Bun versions. Consider restricting the range to the same major.minor (i.e., allow patch releases only).

`startChromeTrace` writes into `OPENCODE_PERFORMANCE_TRACE_DIR` without ensuring the directory exists, so the first run can fail with ENOENT if the path hasn’t been created yet. Create the directory recursively before starting/stopping tracing.

`testDir: ".."` makes this config discover the entire `e2e` tree. When `OPENCODE_PERFORMANCE=1` is set (so performance tests aren’t ignored), this can unintentionally run smoke/regression tests with the uncapped Chromium flags. If this config is meant to be performance-only, set `testDir` to the current directory and keep the opt-in gate via `testIgnore`.

This paragraph only mentions `TIMELINE_CPU_PROFILE`, but the session-tab benchmark uses `SESSION_TAB_CPU_PROFILE`. As written it’s easy to set the wrong env var and think profiling is broken. Update the docs to name both knobs (and note that the tab-switch CPU profile only runs on the first cold trial).

The trace CLI scripts (`trace:stats`, `trace:inp`, `trace:selectors`) are added to `packages/app/package.json`, so these `bun trace:*` commands need to be run from `packages/app` (or via `bun --cwd packages/app ...`). Saying “The repository pins …” is ambiguous/misleading here.

This file re-implements the URL-safe `base64Encode` helper, but other Playwright specs in this repo import it from `@opencode-ai/core/util/encode`. Duplicating the encoding logic risks subtle drift (e.g. padding/URL-safe transforms) and makes future changes harder.

Consider importing `base64Encode` from the shared util and deleting this local helper.

The “Chrome traces” section implies `OPENCODE_PERFORMANCE_TRACE_DIR` is the knob for trace capture, but `session-timeline-benchmark.spec.ts` uses `TIMELINE_CHROME_TRACE` (a file path) instead. Adding a short note here would help avoid confusion when users try to capture a timeline trace via `OPENCODE_PERFORMANCE_TRACE_DIR` and nothing is emitted.

Suggestion: since `stdout` comes from an external process boundary, this unchecked `JSON.parse` + cast bypasses the style-guide preference for schema decoding untrusted JSON and can throw an unhelpful `SyntaxError` if `az` exits 0 with unexpected output. The human can decide if it is worth tightening, but consider decoding the shape before using `accessToken` / `expiresOn`.
Resolved using Effect Schema for decoding the returned shape and types

Suggestion: for Azure Cognitive Services OAuth, `resourceName` can come from the stored `auth.accountId`, but this provider does not register a `vars` loader like the Azure provider does. Models whose `api.url` contains `${AZURE_COGNITIVE_SERVICES_RESOURCE_NAME}` will only substitute from the process environment, so connecting with OAuth and entering the resource name during `/connect` can still leave the literal placeholder in the base URL. Consider returning a `vars` function that maps the resolved resource name to `AZURE_COGNITIVE_SERVICES_RESOURCE_NAME`.
fixed!

This test reimplements `base64Encode` with `Buffer.from(...)`, but other e2e specs use the shared helper from `@opencode-ai/core/util/encode`. Keeping one implementation avoids subtle encoding drift and keeps tests consistent.

Fixed in 2a6c71e1b by using the shared `base64Encode` helper. I also added a headless submission test that verifies the comment is staged on `review.ts:2` in prompt context without sending a session mutation.
`ServerConnection` is only used in type positions in this module. With `verbatimModuleSyntax: true`, this should be a type-only import to avoid emitting a runtime dependency/import.

`initialMessagePageSize` dropping from 80 to `2` is a surprising behavior change and reads like a magic number. Adding a short comment here would make it clear this is intentional for the new “small opaque cursor page” navigation behavior.

`findIndex` currently calls `matches(samples[index + 1]!)` / `matches(samples[index + 2]!)` without a bounds check. If there is no stable triple, and the last (or next-to-last) sample matches, this will call `matches(undefined)` and throw at runtime.

`TargetSessionRoute` decodes/validates the server route segment twice (once in `conn` and again in the keyed `<Show>`). Since `requireServerKey` does real work and can throw, it’s cleaner to compute the decoded key once (memo) and reuse it for both the connection lookup and the provider keying.

`bun --revision` typically returns only the commit hash (no `canary` marker), so the `grep -q "canary"` check will never pass and the cross-compile pre-cache loop will be skipped even on canary installs. Use `bun --version` (which includes `canary` on canary builds) for the canary check and for extracting the semver prefix.

When ArrowUp/ArrowDown is pressed in the search input and there is no currently checked radio item (e.g. no selected project, or the selected project is filtered out), focus falls back to `contentRef`, not to a menu item. This can leave keyboard navigation in an odd state because focus is on the menu container instead of an item. Prefer focusing the first/last visible radio item as a fallback, and prevent/stop propagation for ArrowUp/Down so Kobalte doesn’t also process the key event from the input.

The new `check` icon uses default stroke caps/joins, which renders noticeably sharper than the existing checkmark used in menu v2 (`packages/ui/src/v2/components/menu-v2.tsx` uses round caps/joins). Adding `stroke-linecap`/`stroke-linejoin` keeps the checkmark consistent across the UI.

Prefer importing the shared `base64Encode` helper from `@opencode-ai/core/util/encode` (used by other app e2e specs) instead of redefining it locally. This keeps URL encoding consistent with the app and avoids duplicated implementations across tests.
After switching to the shared `base64Encode` import, the local `base64Encode` implementation can be removed to avoid duplication and potential drift.

Suggestion: this guard now exempts only issues. The previous code skipped both issues and PRs for OWNER/MEMBER authors in this workflow, so a maintainer-authored PR that still has `needs:compliance` can now be auto-closed after two hours. If PRs should retain the existing exemption, consider applying `isExempt(item)` before the close path as well.

`openapi.json` now includes the `embedding` modality enum, but the generated JS SDK types appear only partially regenerated: `packages/sdk/js/src/gen/types.gen.ts` still defines `modalities.input/output` as Array<"text"|"audio"|"image"|"video"|"pdf"> (no `embedding`). This leaves the v1 JS types out of sync with the OpenAPI/schema change and contradicts the PR description that SDK types were regenerated.

`findByAdmittedSeq` uses `.pipe(Effect.orDie)` which means any DB failure (connection drop, constraint violation, ect) becomes a defect that kills the entire onFailure effect. 

These issues will occurs when that happens
- The original Run.Failed event is never published
- The original failure cause is buried under a new defect
- Downstream observability is completely blind

My suggestion is, wrap the query in a `Effect.catchAll` / `Effect.catchAllDefect` so the event is published even without input context. A partial event is infinitely better than no event


```suggestion
          const input = context.seq === undefined
            ? undefined
            : yield* SessionInput.findByAdmittedSeq(database.db, sessionID, context.seq)
              .pipe(Effect.catchAll(() => Effect.succeed(undefined)))
```

This added diff hunk starts a new `diff --git` section but omits the required `---`/`+++` file headers. Patch application tools (git apply/patch-package/Bun patching) typically require those headers, so this patch may fail to apply even though the hunk itself is valid.

Add `--- a/...` and `+++ b/...` lines before the `@@` header for this section (or alternatively merge this hunk into the earlier `dist/cjs/index.cjs` diff section).

This added diff hunk starts a new `diff --git` section but omits the required `---`/`+++` file headers. Without them, the patch may not apply reliably.

Insert the `---`/`+++` lines before the `@@` header (or merge this hunk into the earlier `dist/esm/index.js` diff section).

This added `src/index.ts` hunk is introduced via a second `diff --git` header but is missing the `---`/`+++` file header lines. That makes the patch format inconsistent with the earlier hunks in this same patch file and can break patch application.

Add the `---`/`+++` lines before the `@@` header (or merge this hunk into the earlier `src/index.ts` diff section).

README introduction was changed to claim this repo exists to solve the Home/End issue, and the added HTML is malformed (`<h1>` is not closed; line 3 repeats `<h1>`). This appears unrelated to the project README and will render incorrectly; please remove this block (or replace with a properly closed heading if you intended to add a project title).
This line leaves trailing whitespace and removes the explicit initializer without adjusting formatting. Please keep it consistent with the rest of the file and drop the trailing space.

persisted() currently returns the stored window ID list without de-duplicating it. If the persisted data ever contains duplicates (e.g. from manual edits or corruption), restoreMainWindows() can create multiple windows with the same id, which will collide on per-window state files and cause registry.register() to overwrite the previous window in the map.

removeStoreFile() deletes whatever path results from join(userData, name). Without guarding against path separators or ".." segments, a malformed name could escape the userData directory and delete unintended files. Adding a simple validation makes this helper safer for future callers.

The comment says the route is keyed only by session ID, but `TargetSessionRoute` is keyed by `${params.serverKey}\0${params.id}`. This is minor, but it’s misleading documentation for why `onMount` is safe here (the component remounts on either serverKey or id changes).

Optional coverage enhancement: since the Windows directory-spelling regression in #34842 was fixed in both `/session` and `/experimental/session`, consider asserting the same spellings against `ExperimentalPaths.session` here as well to prevent the two handlers drifting over time.

Optional coverage enhancement: if you want parity with the `/experimental/session` handler (also touched by the original Windows regression), add an assertion that the created drive-root session is returned from `ExperimentalPaths.session` when queried with the same `/` sentinel.

The mocked SSE endpoints ("/global/event" and "/event") return a cross-origin `text/event-stream` response without CORS headers. Since the app is requesting these from `serverA/serverB` while the page origin is different, browsers will treat the response as a CORS violation, which can cause noisy errors and potential flakiness (retries) during the test run.

The verb-cycling interval is started even when animations are disabled (the component renders the fallback text, but the 3s timer still runs and the displayed verb will still change). If `animations_enabled` is intended as a reduced-motion/animation toggle, the verb rotation should be disabled too.

When `verbs` is provided, `Spinner` ignores its children and replaces the entire label with the cycling verb. In this header, that means the in-progress title (`"Thinking: " + props.title`) disappears as soon as users enable `spinner_verbs`, which is a behavioral regression for titled reasoning steps.

`window.api.setBackgroundColor` ultimately calls Electron's `BrowserWindow.setBackgroundColor`, which expects a hex color string (e.g. `#080808` / `#fafafa`). `getComputedStyle(...).backgroundColor` returns an `rgb(...)` string, which can cause the IPC handler to pass an invalid color to Electron (potentially breaking the background sync or throwing).
If `setBackgroundColor` is updated to pass Electron-compatible hex colors (e.g. `#080808`), this assertion should match the expected hex value instead of `rgb(...)`.

The injected banner contains an ESM `import` statement, so it implicitly relies on the main Rollup output being ESM. Since `main.build.rollupOptions.output.format` is not set here, a future electron-vite/Rollup default change (or a later config edit) could flip the output to CJS and turn this banner into a syntax error. Set `format: "es"` explicitly alongside the banner to make this dependency explicit and stable.

Imports are interleaved with runtime constants (reviewTabID/reviewTabPanelID). Many bundlers/lint setups require imports to be grouped at the top of the module; keeping these constants after the import block avoids potential lint/build issues and preserves consistent module structure.

Array.prototype.toReversed() is a relatively new JS feature and may not be available in all target browsers without a polyfill/transpile step. Using slice().reverse() keeps the same behavior with broader runtime compatibility.

rangeExtractor currently does a linear scan (rows().findIndex) to keep the focused row mounted. This runs during virtualization calculations and can become costly for large trees. Consider precomputing an index-by-path map so the lookup is O(1).

virtualizer.getVirtualItems() is called twice to derive keys and a key->item map, which duplicates work on every virtualizer update. Memoizing the virtual items once and deriving both from it avoids extra allocations.

rangeExtractor does props.files.indexOf(path) to keep the focused row mounted. That is O(n) and can become expensive for large filtered lists. Consider precomputing a path->index map so focus retention stays O(1).

virtualizer.getVirtualItems() is called twice to derive keys and a key->item map, duplicating work and allocations on updates. Memoizing the virtual items once and deriving both from it keeps the hot path tighter.

`onPointerDown` marks a scroll gesture for any pointer button, including right/middle clicks. Also `onPointerMove` can call `setUi("scrollGesture", Date.now())` on every move event during a drag, which can create a high-frequency reactive update loop. Gate to primary button interactions and refresh the gesture timestamp only when the current gesture window has elapsed.

The fixed `waitForTimeout(1_500)` makes this test more timing-dependent and can be flaky under CI load. Prefer waiting on the actual signal (selection length increasing) via `expect.poll`, similar to the scroll assertion below.

`activeReviewFile` is a plain function that recomputes `reviewDiffs()` and scans `diffs` on every call. It’s referenced multiple times in render/props, so this can trigger redundant work each reactive update. Consider memoizing it so it only recalculates when `reviewDiffs()` or `reviewFile()` change.

The lazy diff load promise chain has no `.catch()`. If `loadDiff` ever rejects (now or in a future call site), this effect will produce an unhandled promise rejection. Handle the rejection explicitly (and optionally log) so the component is resilient to network/SDK failures.

The `loadDiff(...).then(...)` chain has no rejection handling. If `loadDiff` rejects (network error, aborted request, etc.), this will surface as an unhandled promise rejection in the app. Add a `.catch(...)` (optionally gated by the same `token` check) to swallow/log failures safely.

`filterControls` is always set to `resultsID`, which makes the sidebar filter input render with combobox + `aria-controls`. However the element with `id={resultsID}` only exists when `SessionFileListV2` is rendered (non-loading and with results). In the default file-tree view, and in loading/empty states, `aria-controls` points to a non-existent element, which breaks the ARIA combobox contract.

`FileTabContent` no longer passes the sizing class(es) onto `Tabs.Content`. `SessionFileView` relies on `h-full`/`min-h-0` ancestors for the `ScrollView class="h-full"` to size correctly; without a height-constrained tab content container, the file view can lose its intended scroll/height behavior in the side panel.

While `props.placeholder` is true, `sidebarOpened()` is forced to `true`, but the sidebar toggle still calls `props.state.toggleSidebar`. Clicking the toggle during the placeholder state will flip the persisted `sidebarOpened` preference without any visible UI change, and when leaving the placeholder the sidebar may unexpectedly end up opened (or closed) due to that hidden preference change. Consider hiding or disabling the toggle while the placeholder is active to prevent accidental state changes that the user can’t observe.

The MCP/LSP status unions are duplicated here. Since the app already depends on the SDK types, this can drift if new status values are added upstream; deriving the string unions from `@opencode-ai/sdk/v2/client` avoids that maintenance risk.

The warp flow stashes changes in the source workspace, but then immediately calls `vcs.stashPop` against the *source* workspace after a successful warp. That restores the just-stashed changes right away (so nothing is preserved for “return”), which contradicts the intended “stash on leave, pop on return” behavior.
